name: GST Invoice Reconciler - GSTR-2B Upload, Carry-forward ITC Tracking & Tiered Vendor Escalation

parameters.content:
## 1. Triggers & rules
Monthly run at 10 AM on the 15th (GSTR-2B is generated on the 14th), or immediately after a GSTR-2B upload. Return period comes from the uploaded file, otherwise defaults to last month. Tolerances, confidence threshold and deadline warning window live in **Set Recon Rules**.

## 1b. GSTR-2B upload (form)
Upload the **JSON** from GST portal > Returns > GSTR-2B > Download. B2B and B2BA invoices are written to the GSTR-2B tab, keyed on period + GSTIN + invoice, so re-uploads update rows.
**GSTR-2B headers:** Row Key, Return Period, Section, Supplier GSTIN, Supplier Name, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, Invoice Value, Taxable Value, IGST, CGST, SGST, Cess, ITC Available, Reason, Supplier Filing Date, Uploaded On

## 2. History & mailbox
Reads the Reconciliation tab once. PDFs already reconciled in an earlier period are skipped before any AI call, and open items are counted for carry-forward. Then searches Gmail and splits each new PDF attachment into its own item.

## 3. AI extraction & validation
GPT extracts supplier GSTIN, invoice number, date, tax split and a confidence score. The validator enforces the GSTIN mod-36 check digit, tax arithmetic, CGST = SGST, and IGST vs CGST/SGST by state code. Failures, scans and low-confidence reads become **Needs Manual Review**.

## 4. Reconcile vs GSTR-2B
Exact, then fuzzy matching. Earlier open items are re-checked against the new 2B. Adds Section 16(4) deadline (30 Nov after the FY), days left and priority (Lapsed / Critical / High / Normal). Results upsert on Recon Key.
**Reconciliation headers:** Recon Key, Return Period, Last Checked Period, Vendor Name, Vendor GSTIN, Vendor Email, Invoice Number, Invoice Date, Book Tax, GSTR-2B Tax, GSTR-2B Invoice No, Difference, ITC at Risk, Status, Action, Priority, ITC Deadline, Days to Deadline, Carried Forward, First Flagged, Source, Message ID, Thread ID, Checked On
**Manual Review headers:** Review Key, Return Period, Vendor, Sender Email, File, Reason, Gmail Link, Logged On, Resolved

## 5. Summary & approval
The accounts team gets a report with this period's issues, carried-forward items, late-reported items now claimable, manual-review items and 2B entries with no invoice. If any vendor needs chasing, an approval email waits up to 48 hours. No response or decline means reminders are saved as drafts.

## 6. Tiered vendor follow-ups
One reminder per vendor covering this period and older open invoices. Tier 1 friendly, tier 2 firm (or any Section 16(4)-critical item), tier 3 final notice. Approved runs reply in the original invoice thread with accounts in CC; otherwise drafts.
**Vendor Follow-ups headers:** Vendor GSTIN, Vendor Name, Vendor Email, Reminder Count, Current Tier, Last Reminded, Last Period, Open ITC at Risk, Last Action
Reset a vendor's Reminder Count to 0 once they are clean.

## 7. Payment-hold escalation
Vendors on a final notice are bundled into one email to accounts recommending that the GST portion of pending payments is held until the invoices appear in GSTR-2B.

values.content: You write emails from an Indian business's accounts team to a supplier about GST input tax credit problems. Match the tone to the tier. Tier 1 (friendly reminder): polite and helpful. Tier 2 (firm follow-up): courteous but direct, note this is a follow-up and that unresolved items may affect payment of the GST portion. Tier 3 (final notice): formal, state that the GST portion of pending payments will be held until the invoices appear correctly in our GSTR-2B. Never accusatory. For 'Missing in GSTR-2B' ask them to report the invoice in GSTR-1 or IFF and share the filing acknowledgement. For 'Tax Mismatch' ask them to amend the tax in GSTR-1. For 'GSTIN Issue', 'Billed to Wrong GSTIN' or 'Wrong Tax Type' ask for a corrected invoice or amendment. For 'ITC Blocked in GSTR-2B' ask them to check the place of supply and invoice details they reported. If there are items from earlier periods, list them separately as still pending. If a Section 16(4) deadline is given, mention the date. List invoices exactly as given, mention the total ITC at risk, ask for action before the next GSTR-1 due date on the 11th. Under 200 words, plain text, no bracketed placeholders, sign off as 'Accounts Team' followed by the company name. Return only JSON: {"subject": "...", "body": "..."}

parameters.content:
# GST Invoice Reconciler (Gmail vs GSTR-2B) with carry-forward, escalation and approval

Input tax credit only counts once the supplier reports the invoice in GSTR-1. Most teams find the gaps while filing GSTR-3B, when it is too late to chase anyone, and last month's gaps are forgotten. This workflow reconciles every purchase invoice in your inbox against GSTR-2B, keeps chasing open items month after month, and escalates vendors who ignore reminders.

## How it works
1. **Two entry points.** Upload the GSTR-2B JSON from the GST portal through a form (it is parsed straight into your sheet and the run starts), or let the monthly schedule use whatever is already in the GSTR-2B tab.
2. **History first.** Past results are loaded so PDFs reconciled in earlier periods are not sent to AI again.
3. **AI extraction with validation.** GPT reads each invoice PDF. Code then checks the GSTIN check digit, that tax components add up, IGST vs CGST/SGST against the place of supply, and the model's confidence. Scanned or doubtful invoices go to a Manual Review tab instead of being guessed.
4. **Reconciliation.** Exact match on GSTIN and invoice number, then fuzzy matching (edit distance + amount). Flags missing invoices, tax mismatches, ITC blocked in 2B, wrong tax type and wrong billed-to GSTIN. Open items from earlier months are re-checked and marked resolved when the vendor reports late. Each item gets a Section 16(4) deadline and a priority.
5. **Approval.** Accounts get a summary, then an approve/decline email. Approved reminders are sent as replies in the original invoice thread, otherwise saved as Gmail drafts.
6. **Escalation.** A follow-up log counts reminders per vendor: friendly, then firm, then final notice. Vendors on their third reminder trigger a payment-hold recommendation to accounts.

## Setup steps
1. Create one Google Sheet with tabs **GSTR-2B**, **Reconciliation**, **Manual Review** and **Vendor Follow-ups**, add the header rows listed in the section notes, and paste the sheet ID into every Sheets node.
2. Connect Gmail, Google Sheets and OpenAI credentials.
3. Fill in company name, GSTIN, accounts email and thresholds in **Set Recon Rules**.
4. Activate the workflow (the form and the approval email need it active), then open the form URL and upload a GSTR-2B JSON for a first run.
5. Decline the first approval so you can review the drafts before ever sending.

## Credentials & security
OAuth2 for Gmail and Google Sheets, API key for OpenAI. Invoice text is sent to OpenAI for extraction, so confirm that fits your data policy and keep the sheet restricted. The approval step means nothing reaches a vendor without a human click.

values.content: You extract data from Indian GST purchase invoices. Return only JSON with keys: isTaxInvoice (boolean; false for quotations, proforma invoices, statements, payment receipts, credit or debit notes), vendorName, vendorGSTIN (the supplier's 15-character GSTIN), buyerGSTIN (the billed-to GSTIN), invoiceNumber (exactly as printed), invoiceDate (YYYY-MM-DD), taxableValue, igst, cgst, sgst, cess, totalTax, totalAmount, confidence (0 to 1, how sure you are that GSTIN, invoice number and tax amounts are read correctly). Amounts are plain numbers with no commas or currency symbols. Use 0 for a tax that is not charged and null for anything unreadable. Never guess a GSTIN; if it is unclear return null and lower the confidence.
